newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas extends week-long losses.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas extends week-long losses.

text.p: Gasoline extended week-long losses, with traders who previously bought turning into sellers on Wednesday, while other sellers were sidelined with the rise in crude and naphtha.
Unleaded 95-Ron gasoline prices have fallen by nearly $2.00 since April 2, when it was quoted at $27.60.

A Japanese trader who bought one million barrels in March and around 150,000 barrels in April, and a Dutch trader who bought 50,000 barrels on Tuesday, emerged as sellers offering the 95-octane at $25.70 and $25.90 per barrel, fob Singapore.
The grade was traded on Tuesday at $25.80.
But the European major who sold the cargo was more cautious amid the lack of buyers.
"With naphtha and crude going up, I don't want to be so aggressive on the mogas," the trader said.
Naphtha swaps firmed for the second day, with May quoted at $21.70/$21.90 per barrel from $21.55/$21.65 on Tuesday.
Talk on the physical market was thin.
"There is not much demand in May while no sellers are showing any cargoes," a trader said.
Traders said premiums for fob Singapore barrels lifting in May were assessed at around 60-70 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes.

On tenders, Rayong Refinery Co Ltd sold 230,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline to Shell Singapore at around $1.00 per barrel below Singapore 95-octane spot quotes, fob Thailand lifting April 17, industry sources said.
The tender closed April 8 and was valid for the same day.
